primary_citation.popular_name: Authentication of a Writing — California state-court analog to FRE 901; the legal embodiment of SOC-001 / Authentic Identity

structural_location.chapter: CHAPTER 1. Authentication and Proof of Writings [1400 - 1454]
structural_location.section_history: Enacted by Stats. 1965, Ch. 299. NEVER AMENDED — the section is in its original 1965 form, unchanged for 60+ years.

verbatim_text.verbatim_full: Authentication of a writing means (a) the introduction of evidence sufficient to sustain a finding that it is the writing that the proponent of the evidence claims it is or (b) the establishment of such facts by any other means provided by law.

structural_breakdown.method_a: (a) the introduction of evidence sufficient to sustain a finding that it is the writing that the proponent of the evidence claims it is — meaning extrinsic evidence (testimony, comparison, distinctive characteristics, business-record foundation, etc.) sufficient to support a reasonable jury finding that the writing is what its proponent says it is
structural_breakdown.method_b: (b) the establishment of such facts by any other means provided by law — meaning any statutory or judicial mechanism for treating a writing as authenticated (self-authentication categories, judicial notice, presumption, admission, stipulation, etc.)
structural_breakdown.doctrinal_significance: § 1400 is the foundational definition of 'authentication' for California state court purposes. Every writing offered into evidence in California state court must be authenticated under § 1400 (or fall within a self-authentication category in §§ 1450-1454). This is the California state-court equivalent of FRE 901 in federal court. Both are operational forms of the SOC-001 / Authentic Identity doctrine: a writing must be what it claims to be, and the proponent must prove it.

amendment_history.event: Original enactment as part of the entire Evidence Code recodification of 1965. The 1965 Evidence Code replaced the prior Code of Civil Procedure evidence provisions and brought California evidence law into a unified code.
amendment_history.primary_source_status: NOT YET FETCHED — would require 1965 Vol1 California Statutes PDF

amendment_history_note: § 1400 has NEVER been amended since its 1965 enactment. The text is in its original form. This is unusual for a 60-year-old California section and reflects the foundational, structural nature of the provision.

steward_case_relevance_audit.purpose: Map § 1400 against the steward's case file. § 1400 is the rule the steward will rely on to authenticate every writing he wants to use as evidence in any California state court proceeding. It is also the rule under which any opposing party's writing must be authenticated. The audit asks: which writings in the steward's case file are properly authenticated under § 1400, which are not, and which ones the opposing parties have used were never properly authenticated either?
steward_case_relevance_audit.audit_filed_by: Claude (assistant) at first-mouth level; steward review required

factor_audits.factor_id: Method (a) — extrinsic evidence sufficient to sustain a finding
factor_audits.what_the_statute_requires: The proponent of a writing must introduce extrinsic evidence (testimony, expert opinion, comparison samples, distinctive characteristics, chain of custody, etc.) sufficient to support a reasonable juror in finding that the writing is what the proponent claims it is. The standard is permissive — sufficient TO SUSTAIN A FINDING, not proof beyond a reasonable doubt and not a preponderance.
factor_audits.what_the_record_shows: The steward's case file includes many writings whose authenticity is contested. Particularly: the 6/11/2009 Oakland Police Department report (per project_christina_pattern.md, the October 2025 OPD records pickup confirmed the related 6/2/2009 OPD report does not exist in the OPD records system); the 19 unsigned documents in the 2958 Honeysuckle sale (per project_house_sale_fraud.md); various medical records with documented gaps and inconsistencies (per project_medical_fraud_timeline.md).
factor_audits.audit_question: For each contested writing in the steward's case file, can the proponent who introduced it actually satisfy § 1400(a)? If the OPD records system does not contain the document the opposing party offered as a 'police report,' what extrinsic evidence supports the finding that the document is what they claimed it was?
factor_audits.audit_status: CRITICAL — directly load-bearing. § 1400 is the gate every contested writing must pass. The OPD records pickup is itself the steward's § 1400 disprove evidence: the agency that purportedly issued the document does not have it in its records system.

factor_audits.factor_id: Method (b) — establishment by other means provided by law
factor_audits.what_the_statute_requires: Authentication may also be accomplished by any other statutory or judicial mechanism — self-authentication under §§ 1450-1454, presumption under §§ 1450, judicial admission, stipulation, prior court order, etc.
factor_audits.audit_question: Have any of the contested writings been authenticated by stipulation, prior court order, or self-authentication under §§ 1450-1454? If a writing is being treated as authenticated by stipulation or admission, that stipulation/admission can be the focal point of challenge.
factor_audits.audit_status: FLAGGED — secondary path. Most case-file writings will rely on Method (a).

factor_audits.what_the_statute_requires: The proponent of a writing bears the burden of authentication. If the proponent fails to satisfy § 1400, the writing is inadmissible. The opposing party does NOT bear the burden of disproving authenticity.
factor_audits.what_the_record_shows: In litigation involving the steward, the burden allocation under § 1400 has structural significance: when an opposing party offers a contested writing, THEY have the burden to authenticate it. The steward does not have to prove the writing is fake; the proponent has to prove it is real.
factor_audits.audit_question: In each instance where an opposing party introduced a writing the steward disputes, was the proponent put to their § 1400 burden? Or was the writing admitted without authentication on stipulation, default, or judicial inattention?
factor_audits.audit_status: CRITICAL — structural rule. § 1400's burden allocation is a procedural lever the steward can exercise in any state-court proceeding involving a contested writing.

steward_case_relevance_audit.audit_summary: TWO CRITICAL audit items: (1) for each contested writing, can the proponent satisfy § 1400(a) with extrinsic evidence? Where the agency that purportedly issued a document does not have the document in its records, § 1400(a) cannot be satisfied — the OPD records pickup IS the disproving evidence. (2) Burden allocation — the proponent has the burden, not the steward. Procedurally, the steward (or his counsel) should object to admission of any contested writing on § 1400 grounds and require the proponent to make the threshold authentication showing. The 1965 enactment date and the section's never-being-amended posture mean § 1400 is rock-stable doctrine that any California trial judge will recognize and enforce.
